'''''Salacia chinensis''''' is a species of [[plant]] in the family [[Celastraceae]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Contributions from the United States National Herbarium|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YbsmAQAAIAAJ|year=2003|publisher=Smithsonian Institution Press|pages=192–}}</ref> A climbing [[shrub]], it is also known as '''Chinese salacia''', '''lolly berry''',<ref name="JanickPaull2008">{{cite book|author1=Jules Janick|author2=Robert E. Paull|title=The Encyclopedia of Fruit and Nuts|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cjHCoMQNkcgC&pg=PA417|year=2008|publisher=CABI|isbn=978-0-85199-638-7|pages=417–}}</ref> and '''saptachakra''' in [[Ayurveda]].<ref name="Khare2004">{{cite book|author=C.P. Khare|title=Indian Herbal Remedies: Rational Western Therapy, Ayurvedic, and Other Traditional Usage, Botany|url=https://archive.org/details/springer_10.1007-978-3-642-18659-2|year=2004|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-540-01026-5|pages=[https://archive.org/details/springer_10.1007-978-3-642-18659-2/page/n409 410]–}}</ref> The plant is found widespread in South-East Asia and [[Australoceania]].

==Description==
Leaves are elliptic, narrowly ovate-round or obovate-elliptic 4.2-10.5 cm long and 2.2-4.0 cm wide, and glabrous; the [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] are 5–8 mm long. The [[fruit]] has one seed in it, the seed is only 8 mm long. [[Flowers]] have five petals and they are [[yellow]] or yellowish-green.
